newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo government imposes cigarette, alcohol stamps.
newsitem.headline: Yugo government imposes cigarette, alcohol stamps.

text.p: The Yugoslav government adopted a regulation on Friday introducing compulsory tax stamps on all tobacco and alcohol in a bid to stifle illegal trade, Tanjug news agency reported.

Producers and importers of alcoholic beverages and cigarettes will put unified tax stamps on their products in the entire territory of Yugoslavia, comprising Serbia and Montenegro, the report quoted the federal information secretariat as saying.
On import of goods, authorised importers and consignment warehouses will be directly supplied with the tax stamps.
Yugoslav Customs Administration head Mihalj Kertes in May announced a clampdown on illegal trade which blossomed during years of war-related international sanctions.
According to some estimates, grey economy accounts for up to 40 percent of the country's gross domestic product. -- Beti Bilandzic, Belgrade newsroom 381 11 311 4305
